raw.query: SELECT window_name, rho, MIN(p99_ms) AS min_p99, MAX(p99_ms) AS max_p99 FROM provenance.current_factorial WHERE policy='forecast' AND quantile='p90' AND actuation='issue-time' GROUP BY window_name, rho ORDER BY window_name, rho;
raw.observed: At rho=15, burst1/3/4/5 invariant p99=588.37 ms and steady24h max p99=733.643 ms. At rho=25, burst1/3/4/5 max p99 reaches 677.461-904.739 ms and steady24h max p99 reaches 995.058 ms. burst2 and burst6 are missing.
raw.claimed: p90 policy holds its per-window p99 unchanged across leads from L=15 to 165 s at the 588 ms service floor on every burst window and feasible (below 734 ms) on the calm day.
raw.evidence: The claim holds only in simulation (current_factorial) under the narrow tuning subset rho=15 for tested burst windows (burst1/3/4/5). It misses burst2/6 entirely, fails under other valid tuning parameters (e.g. rho=25 calm day reaches 995 ms), and is violated by physical validation measurements (v_pool_latency burst1 has a p99 of 598.74 ms due to real-world overheads).
raw.fix: Qualify that lead-invariance at 588 ms and calm-day feasibility below 734 ms hold specifically for the simulated rho=15 subset of tested burst windows (burst1/3/4/5), and acknowledge that physical measurements or other tuning configurations exceed these bounds.
